backlog.spec: After the basin-hopping loop ends, and only once, re-run SLSQP from the unperturbed best centres and 0.999 * best radii with options maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-13, then clip, repair and keep the result only if its radius sum is larger than the incumbent's. This recovers the small slack left by the default ftol=1e-6 stopping and by the repair shrink, without paying the tight tolerance on every hop. Reserve time for it by ending the hop loop 1.5 s earlier than now.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: Give _solve_once an optional argument r0=None. When it is given, use x0 = concatenate([centers0.ravel(), r0]) in place of the constant INIT_RADIUS. In the basin-hopping loop, pass r0 = 0.9 * best radii, so that SLSQP starts from the incumbent radius pattern, which is near-feasible after the perturbation, and not from equal small radii. The restart phase stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Warm-start radii in hops

backlog.spec: Lower HOP_SD from 0.04 to 0.025 so that each hop explores closer to the incumbent. This is about half of a typical radius (~0.09). With smaller hops, more of them should land in nearby, slightly better basins rather than in worse, distant ones. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Smaller basin-hopping perturbation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep the current packing as a separate state from best. Accept a new local optimum into the current state whenever its radius sum is within 1e-6 of the current state's sum, even when it is slightly worse than best, so the chain can drift across degenerate optima of equal sum. Always update best when a strictly higher sum is found. The hop perturbation and the SLSQP and repair steps are unchanged. Note that this is a schedule of acceptance, not a new hop move.
backlog.title: Plateau-drift acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that places circles on two or three concentric square rings inside the unit square, with a random number of circles per ring (summing to n), a random ring offset in [0, 0.05], and a random angular phase per ring. Add small Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 and clip to the box, then pass the start through _relax. Roughly a third of the restart pool uses this generator; the rest stays uniform random. This targets layered packings that uniform random starts rarely reach.
backlog.title: Concentric ring-layer starts

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, add noise with sd 3*HOP_SD to the centres of the 8 smallest-radius circles in the best packing and sd 0.3*HOP_SD to the others, since small circles sit in loose holes whose arrangement matters most.
backlog.title: Radius-ordered hop: perturb only small circles

backlog.spec: Remove the four wall-constraint blocks and the r>=0 block from cons, and pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Keep the pair-distance constraints, plus add wall constraints only as c-r>=0 forms if needed for validity. The repair step still guarantees validity. This shrinks the constraint count and speeds up SLSQP, giving more restarts.
backlog.title: Wall bounds via SLSQP bounds

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the Gaussian perturbation rng.normal(0, HOP_SD, c.shape) with a Student-t perturbation with 2 degrees of freedom: 0.5 * HOP_SD * rng.standard_t(2, c.shape), clipped elementwise to [-0.3, 0.3], and clip the perturbed centres to [0.02, 0.98] before the solve. Most circles then barely move while a few make large jumps, which mixes local refinement and occasional rearrangement of one or two circles in a single move type.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed hop noise

backlog.spec: Make POOL depend on the restart round index: round k uses pool size min(40, 10 * 2**(k-1)), and KEEP stays at 3. Early rounds are cheap and explore many starts, and later rounds spend more relaxations on the same budget. The round index is counted from 0 in the restart phase, and the hop phase is unchanged. Only the pool size varies across rounds.
backlog.title: Growing restart pool schedule

backlog.spec: Change the restart-round sizing from POOL = 20, KEEP = 3 to POOL = 60, KEEP = 1. The cheap L-BFGS relaxations are a small fraction of the cost of an SLSQP solve, so this makes each SLSQP solve start from the best of 60 relaxed configurations instead of the top 3 of 20, at roughly the same number of SLSQP solves per second. Only the two constants change.
backlog.title: Wider relaxed pool, fewer refinements per round

backlog.spec: Re-implement the slot 16 change: in the random-restart pool, build half of the start configurations mirror-symmetric about x=0.5. Draw n//2 centres uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 0.5] x [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], append their mirror images (1-x, y), and when n is odd add one centre on x=0.5 at a uniform y. Then relax these starts with _relax like the others. The other half stays uniform. This is meant to confirm the -2.9386 single run.
backlog.title: Replicate mirror-symmetric starts (slot 16)

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed top-KEEP selection in each restart round with a seeded random draw. Sample KEEP distinct starts from the pool with probability proportional to exp(-(E - E_min) / T), where E is the relaxed energy and T is set to the median energy of the pool. The best-energy start stays guaranteed in the sample. This keeps some diversity among restart starts while still favouring low-energy relaxations.
backlog.title: Stochastic selection among pool starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop of solve, do not add Gaussian noise to every centre. Draw k = rng.integers(3, 9) distinct circle indices with rng.choice(n, k, replace=False) and add rng.normal(0, 2*HOP_SD, (k, 2)) only to those centres. Clip the result to [0, 1] and then call _solve_once as before. All other circles start exactly at their best positions, so the hop is local but larger for the chosen circles.
backlog.title: Perturb only a random subset of centres per hop

backlog.spec: During basin-hopping SLSQP solves only (not the random-restart solves), pass scipy bounds that limit each variable to a box of half-width 0.12 around the perturbed start, for both centres and radii, with radii also bounded below by 0. Keep the wall and non-overlap constraints as they are. The box acts as a local trust region that stops the solver from jumping to distant basins during a hop. Restarts keep unbounded variables.
backlog.title: Trust-box bounds on hop solves

backlog.spec: For half of the random restart draws, generate n/2 random centres in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and add their reflections through (0.5, 0.5), giving an exactly point-symmetric start. Use n-odd handling by placing the last circle at the centre. Relax the symmetric start with _relax as usual, so the pool contains both symmetric and unconstrained candidates. The SLSQP stage itself is unchanged and no symmetry is enforced after the start.
backlog.title: C2 point-symmetric restart starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, let _solve_once take an optional starting radius vector, and with probability 0.5 start the hop from the unperturbed best centres plus small Gaussian noise of sd 0.01, with radii set to 1.08 times the best radii, i.e. a deliberately overlapping, over-inflated state. SLSQP must then resolve the overlaps by pushing circles apart, which tends to change the contact graph in the tightest regions instead of moving every circle randomly. The other half of the hops stay as the current Gaussian hop with INIT_RADIUS radii.
backlog.title: Overpressure hop start

backlog.spec: Combine the two unconfirmed -2.9386 changes. (a) Half of the restart pool starts are mirror-symmetric about x=0.5, as in slot 16: n//2 centres in the left half, mirrored to (1-x, y). (b) Before each SLSQP solve in both phases, as in slot 34, run 10 short steps of the cheap penalty relax (call _relax with options maxiter=10) on the start centres to remove gross overlaps. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-best combo: mirror starts plus pre-solve grid nudge

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so the basin-hopping phase gets about 16% more hops. To stay safe against the 45 s void limit, track the longest single _solve_once duration seen so far (measured with time.process_time) and, in both loops of solve, break out as soon as the remaining time before TIME_FRACTION * time_limit is less than 1.5 times that longest duration. HOP_START stays 0.4, so the restart phase also scales up. No other change.
backlog.title: Use more of the time budget with a solve-duration guard

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, call _repair only when the raw SLSQP radius sum (before repair) is at least best sum minus 0.002. Otherwise discard the candidate without repairing it. Repair is the most expensive per-hop step, so this frees time for more hops. Candidates that pass the filter get the same repair and best-update logic as before, so every stored packing is still valid.
backlog.title: Lazy repair on promising hop results

memo: Helped: two changes. Slot 3 (pool of 20 random starts relaxed cheaply, best refined) gave -2.9308/-2.9317. Slot 8 (perturbing the best packing after the first 40% of the budget) gave -2.9375/-2.9365, now the incumbent at -2.9370, about the published ~2.9370. Nothing since has beaten it beyond noise (sd ~0.0034). Did not help: two-tier restarts (-2.9204), perturb-and-repair (-2.9204), single-pass repair (-2.9246), greedy growth (-2.9331), hex seeding (-2.9355), warm starts (-2.9356), torus lattice (-2.9356). Within noise at -2.9375: MAX_ITER 1000, analytic Jacobians, best-of-4 hops, LP polish, shear hop, dimer move, centroid scaling. Unconfirmed single runs: slot 16 mirror-symmetric starts (-2.9386), slots 34 and 35 (-2.9386 each). Slot 21 crashed. Next: replicate slots 16, 34 and 35, since a gain of 0.0015 is still within noise. Then tune slot 8's knobs (40% split, perturbation size, circles moved) and the slot 3 pool size. Avoid more repair variants and new hop moves.
